draft.title: Peer review and replication
card: Scientists publish their methods and results in journals. Other people can then see exactly what was done and how the conclusions were reached.
before a journal publishes a study, independent experts in the same field read it. They check whether the methods suit the question and whether the results support the conclusions.
after publication, other scientists repeat the investigation using the published methods. If they get similar results, confidence in the finding grows.
An idea becomes accepted when evidence from many independent teams builds a consensus among scientists. Even then, it can still change with new evidence.
draft.remember: Checks by other experts, in review and by repeating the work, build confidence in a finding, but it can still change.

a.q: A journal article lists the methods as well as the results. Why is this done?
opts: So other scientists can check and repeat the work
So other scientists can claim the findings as theirs
So the results can skip any further testing
So the journal can decide which topics get studied
a.why: Published methods let other experts judge whether the work was sound and repeat it to see if they get similar results. Publishing does not end testing: even well-checked findings can change when new evidence appears.
a.clue: Think about what another scientist needs in order to repeat a study.

b.q: Dr Nguyen in Melbourne publishes a study finding that a new feed helps hens lay more eggs. A team in Bendigo follows her published methods and gets similar results. Which step is this, and what does it do?
opts: Replication, which builds confidence in her finding
Peer review, which builds confidence in her finding
Replication, which means no more testing is needed
Peer review, which means no more testing is needed
b.why: Repeating a published study with similar results is replication, and it builds confidence in the finding. Peer review is the check by experts before publication, so it is a different step. No check ends testing, because new evidence can still change a finding.
b.clue: Did the Bendigo team check the work before or after it was published?

a.best: So other scientists can check and repeat the work

b.best: Replication, which builds confidence in her finding
